 Tax Average tax rate drops 4% 
 By Daniel Hood CloseText About Daniel 
 twitter accountingedit 
 mailto daniel.hood@arizent.com 
 linkedin daniel-hood-3494ab49 
 Published November 09, 2026, 2:14 p.m. EST | Updated November 09, 2026, 2:32 p.m. EST 1 Min Read Facebook 
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Email 
 IRS CEO Frank Bisignano Tierney L. Cross/Bloomberg What's at Stake: Taxpayers and businesses navigating the administration's move to eliminate paper-based payments.
 Supporting Data: Nearly 250% jump in payments made through business tax accounts.
 With $5.6 trillion in taxes collected and the average tax rate falling 4%, the Internal Revenue Service is touting its performance in fiscal year 2026 as "historic" and "record-setting."
 Processing Content The revenue figure of $5.6 trillion represents an increase of nearly 5% from the previous year, despite the average individual tax rate dropping for all income categories. The overall average tax rate hit 12.6%, according to the IRS, down 4% from 2025.
 Meanwhile, the average refund was up 11%, and approximately 90% of taxpayers who e-filed got their refund in less than 21 days.
 "The IRS delivered to America's working families historic refunds due to the tax cuts enacted in the Working Families Tax Cuts, which represent the cornerstone of the administration's economic agenda," said IRS CEO Frank Bisignano, in a statement. "With our dedicated workforce, we delivered a successful tax filing season and continue to transform the IRS into a digital-first agency that provides the best possible experience for taxpayers, improves collections, and safeguards privacy."
 Taxpayers took greater advantage of IRS resources, the agency reported, with users of Individual Online Accounts hitting 37.6 million, up 34%, and users of Tax Professional Accounts up 57%, to 513,000.
 Visits to IRS.gov hit almost a billion, and taxpayers used the Where's My Refund? functionality nearly 469 million times.
 In keeping with the Trump administration's move to eliminate paper-based payments, payments made through individual online accounts grew 57%, topping $133.6 million, and payments through business tax accounts jumped almost 250%, to $726.6 million.
 In addition, 12% more refunds were issued through direct deposit than in the previous year.
